source.context: TCI page, reference 2). The α-thiocarbocation from the Pummerer reaction of an o-aroyl-substituted sulfoxide is trapped by the adjacent keto oxygen; without a dienophile the paper isolates 4-(ethylthio)-6-phenylthieno[2,3-c]furan. source.context: TCI page, reference 1) (the page prints the volume as 45). First steps of the synthesis: citronellal treated with the ylide from Ph₃P and CBr₄ gives the 1,1-dibromoolefin (98%), and exposure to n-BuLi gives the terminal acetylene (95%). problems.verificationNote: The TCI scheme image could not be downloaded (proxy refusal), so the drawn example 1) was not seen; the structures come from the PMC full text of ref. 1 (citronellal → 1,1-dibromoolefin → terminal alkyne), stereochemistry omitted. The say-my-name.net equation and mechanism images could not be downloaded either. Mechanism is the established one (TCI text gives only the two-step summary): Wittig-type addition of Ph₃P=CBr₂ via betaine/oxaphosphetane, then Br/Li exchange, α-elimination to the vinylidene carbene and Fritsch–Buttenberg–Wiechell 1,2-H shift, deprotonation by the second equivalent of BuLi and aqueous workup. A chemist should check the betaine/oxaphosphetane drawings and the carbene (drawn as [C]=C) in step 2; the alternative pathway (HBr elimination to the bromoalkyne, then Br/Li exchange) is also found in textbooks.

source.context: General equation of the say-my-name.net page (RC(O)R′ + diethyl succinate, base → R(R′)C=C(CO₂Et)CH₂CO₂H) with R = R′ = Me (the equation draws a ketone, so the simplest ketone, acetone, was used) and the unspecified base given as sodium ethoxide (chosen here to match the ethyl esters): diethyl succinate + acetone → 3-(ethoxycarbonyl)-4-methylpent-3-enoic acid. The intermediates follow the page's mechanism image: deprotonation of diethyl succinate (ester enolate); addition of the enolate to the ketone C=O (alkoxide); attack of the alkoxide on the distal ester with loss of EtO⁻ (γ-lactone, ethyl 2,2-dimethyl-5-oxooxolane-3-carboxylate); base-induced ring opening by removal of the α-H (carboxylate of the half-ester). An acidic work-up, not drawn on the page, gives the acid drawn in the equation. The page gives no conditions.

source.context: General equation of the say-my-name.net page (2-arylethylamine with an electron-donating group EDG on the ring + RCHO, H⁺ → 1-R-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline) with EDG = OMe, placed meta to the aminoethyl chain (the page draws the EDG at an unspecified ring position; meta places it para to the ring carbon that is attacked), and R = H (formaldehyde, allowed by the equation): 3-methoxyphenethylamine → 6-methoxy-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline. The intermediates follow the page's mechanism image: condensation of the amine with the aldehyde (− H₂O) to the iminium ion; attack of the ring carbon ortho to the chain on the iminium carbon (6-endo ring closure) to the arenium ion; loss of H⁺ to restore the aromatic ring. The page gives no conditions; aqueous HCl is given here as the acid H⁺.
